quote: 27 acres wheat destroyed, worth $600.00 9 acres Corn 360.00 8 acres Oats 80.00 4 acres Barley 50.00 1 acre Flax 15.00 1 acre Potatoes 50.00 32 acres Grass 650.00 20 tons of Hay out of the barn
says: The Trostle farm petition of 1868: 27 acres of wheat, 9 of corn, 8 of oats, 4 of barley, 1 of flax, 1 of potatoes, 32 of grass and 20 tons of hay in the barn were destroyed.
note: Printed in the National Park Service Civil War Series, The Battle of Gettysburg, section 20 (a petition of Catherine Trostle under the Pennsylvania act of 9 April 1868). The acreage is what she claimed destroyed.

quote: the farm being between the two armies, in part was fought over several times
says: The Trostle farm lay between the two armies and was in part fought over several times; the petition says the crops and fences were totally destroyed.
note: A claimant's statement; 'totally destroyed' is hers. Used as documentation that the fields near the Trostle farm were trampled on 2 July, not for the degree.

quote: that their farm was near Round Top, and was fought over two days, and the crops and fences were totally destroyed
says: The Trostle claim states the farm, near Round Top, was fought over two days and the crops and fences totally destroyed.
